summary:
R4 is the model to lean on today — its strong-play window is scorching at 7d 18-9 (67%, +15.0u) and 14d 36-24 (60%, +14.0u), well clear of R1/R2/R3 which are all sitting in the 53-55% range over 14 days. The catch across every rating is the runs category, cold everywhere (R1 -5.8, R2 -6.8, R3 -5.0, R4 -6.5pts) with 3-4 game losing streaks on every version. Trends remains the anchor category, running 54% over 14d and 56%+ on the season across all four ratings, and trends+sp is the best combo play at 57.0% (315-238, n=553) all year.

Today's board gives 12 of 15 games full four-rating consensus, and the LAD @ CIN game is the headline: all four ratings stack LAD by huge deltas (-3.20 to -3.66), the largest gap on the slate, with Yamamoto on the mound against Rhett Lowder. LAD is also the top team-when-liked play on the season at 31-14 (69%) and elite when it's a strong play — 23-5 (82%, +24.0u) — so this is about as clean a signal as the model produces. TBR @ ATH is the next-strongest consensus, all four ratings on TBR (+1.09 to +2.03), and TBR profiles as one of the model's best teams to back at 35-16 (69%) with a 21-9 strong-play record. BOS @ TEX is a shakier consensus — the delta shrinks to near pick'em (R4 actually flips to -0.83 while R1-R3 barely lean BOS) — worth discounting given BOS's gaudy 39-15 (72%) record demands a real edge, not a coin-flip lean. Watch the three split games (SEA/LAA, DET/TOR, CHW/CLE) — thin, disagreeing deltas under 0.5 across the board, exactly the kind of low-conviction spot where the cold runs category tends to bleed value. Favor plays where trends and sp both point the same direction, and treat CIN and ATH as the top-confidence board plays today.
